label: At D2, fires when S2 is shown, strongly if the last trial was rewarded at S1.
terms: (phase == D2) * (state == S2) ;; (phase == D2) * (state == S2) * (action == 1) ;; (phase == D2) * (state == S2) * (prev_reward == 1) * (prev_state == S1) ;; (phase == D2) * (state == S2) * (prev_reward == 1) ;; (phase == D2) * (state == S2) * belief_lo ;; (phase == D2) * (state == S2) * (tv("reward", -2) == 1)
explanation: Silent at D1 and GO; active only at D2 when the reached state S2 is shown (S1 shown -> zero). Magnitude is set mainly by the previous trial: large when the previous trial was rewarded at S1 (a1 S1 r or a2 S1 r), i.e. S2 arriving after evidence that S1 is good; extra activation when S2 was reached via a rare transition after choosing a1. At D2 the state and this trial choice are already observed, so no future variable is used. The free fit adds a smaller boost for any previous reward, a graded belief_lo term (higher when the observer believes S1 good) and a reward two trials back, giving about 0.05 more dev R^2. Remaining misses are mostly window-first trials where the previous trial is unknown.

issues: The recorded short form is badly set up. With (in_state == 2) as the base term, the fitted weight is -0.04 (dev), so the short form never says 'fires when S2 is shown'. The D2 timing baseline (~0.2) is left on S1 steps, which are predicted at about 0.17 when the actual value is 0. Swapping the base term to (in_state == 1) (weight -0.195), with the other two terms unchanged, raises test R^2 beyond timing from 0.632 to 0.687. That already beats the reported free fit (0.678).

The a1 boost depends on reward. (in_state == 2)*(action == 1) adds only about +0.03 test R^2 to the previous-S1-reward term (0.598 -> 0.632). Restricting it to rewarded previous trials, (in_state == 2)*(action == 1)*(prev_reward == 1), gives 0.728 test. So the rare a1->S2 boost holds mainly after a rewarded trial, which neither the label nor the explanation says.

The label leaves out the a1 / rare-transition component, so a reader cannot predict that a1->S2 after a reward from S2 is also high. The residual table shows this choice x state cell (a1 S2) at +0.86, and the profile's top-residual examples have a1 S2R at about +2.2 after a1 S1 c trials.

Misses on the recorded form: S1 cells at D2 are over-predicted by about 0.17 every time (the baseline artifact). Over-prediction after unrewarded previous trials reaches -0.24 (a1 S2 u). Under the improved form these shrink to at most about 0.13 (after a2 S1 u and a2 S2 u), which is modest next to std 0.31.
The claim that no future variables are used checks out: at D2 the choice and the reached state are both observed.
skeptic.revised_label: D2 only, zero at S1: fires on S2 after a rewarded trial, most if rewarded at S1 or reached by a1.

final_label: D2 only, zero at S1: fires on S2 after a rewarded trial, most if rewarded at S1 or reached by a1.
